source_refs.note: Exercise 10.2 Q11, book p.190 (PDF 195); proof (no key entry). Checked with sympy; solution book PDF 922-923 agrees.

blocks.explanation:
No table is allowed; \(64^{\circ} = 45^{\circ} + 19^{\circ}\) is the key.
Dividing by \(\cos 19^{\circ}\) turns the left side into a tangent-sum shape.
Plan: divide top and bottom by \(\cos 19^{\circ}\), write 1 as \(\tan 45^{\circ}\), use \(\tan(\alpha + \beta)\).
steps:
Given: the identity.
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \tan 64^{\circ}\).
Method:
\[\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{\tan\alpha + \tan\beta}{1 - \tan\alpha\tan\beta}\]
with \(\alpha = 45^{\circ}\), \(\beta = 19^{\circ}\) and \(\tan 45^{\circ} = 1\).

Divide top and bottom by \(\cos 19^{\circ}\)
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{1 + \tan 19^{\circ}}{1 - \tan 19^{\circ}}\]
Why: \(\dfrac{\cos 19^{\circ}}{\cos 19^{\circ}} = 1\) and \(\dfrac{\sin 19^{\circ}}{\cos 19^{\circ}} = \tan 19^{\circ}\).

Write 1 as \(\tan 45^{\circ}\)
\[= \dfrac{\tan 45^{\circ} + \tan 19^{\circ}}{1 - \tan 45^{\circ}\tan 19^{\circ}}\]
Why: \(\tan 45^{\circ} = 1\); this makes the tangent sum formula visible.

Use the formula
\[= \tan(45^{\circ} + 19^{\circ}) = \tan 64^{\circ} = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: Tangent of a sum.
